answer: An agent economy can weight votes by tokens locked for 30 days, not by account count. Splitting 100 tokens across a thousand identities still buys only 100 tokens of voting power, so fake identities add no influence. To gain more, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more capital, bearing its price risk and lost liquidity. Like a harbor in a gale, this rule offers shelter from the fable that a crowd of accounts means a crowd of independent actors.
